He dwelt within the celestial palace of the <term>dharmadhatu</term> <gloss>sphere of reality</gloss>, the essence of non-conceptuality that is far superior to all the three realms. He was together with a great assembly of monks and a vast gathering of <term>bodhisattvas</term> <gloss>beings dedicated to awakening</gloss>, such as: the <term>bodhisattva mahasattva</term> <gloss>great heroic being of awakening</gloss> Non-conceptuality, and Non-conceptual Radiance, and Non-conceptual Moon, and Non-conceptual Hero, and the one skilled in teaching the non-conceptual doctrine, and Non-conceptual Essence, and Non-conceptual <unclear>text ends mid-word</unclear>

<summary>The Buddha resides in the celestial palace of the sphere of reality alongside a vast assembly of monks and specifically named bodhisattvas characterized by non-conceptuality. This passage establishes the divine setting and the high-level spiritual audience for the discourse.</summary>
<keywords>dharmadhatu, non-conceptuality, bodhisattva mahasattva, three realms, celestial palace, Buddhist assembly</keywords>
